author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read IBM i security audit journal (QAUDJRN) entries as CEF, from IBM's DISPLAY_JOURNAL route or Fortra Powertech SIEM Agent for IBM i. Either route sends them over syslog to the data collector. PW entries go to Auth as failed logons, every other T entry goes to CloudAudit, and history log messages and other Powertech events stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- IBM i security audit journal (QAUDJRN) entries are sent as CEF over syslog, by either route.
- IBM's route: an SQL job reads QSYS2.DISPLAY_JOURNAL('QSYS', 'QAUDJRN', GENERATE_SYSLOG => 'RFC5424' or 'RFC3164') and passes SYSLOG_EVENT to the PASE syslog daemon (7.3 and later with the Db2 PTF groups IBM lists).
- IBM's CEF has vendor IBM, product IBM i, the class QSYS-AUDJRN and the name T=<entry type>.
- Fortra Powertech SIEM Agent for IBM i (licensed) in its *CEF style: vendor Powertech, product SIEM Agent, an event ID of T, the entry type and the subtype's place in the alphabet (TPW0016 is PW subtype P), in the current key layout or the older one that packs the job into msg.

Field mapping:
- PW (invalid password or user ID) entries go to Auth as failed logons: the profile that failed from IBM's msg (User JDOE name not valid) or Powertech's event text or DETAIL, the client address, the system as the target, and a failure category from the violation type (P and U incorrect user or password, R expired password, Q and X disabled).
- Every other T entry (AF authority failure, CA, CP, OW, SV and the rest) goes to CloudAudit: the entry's description as the event name, T=<type> as the event type, the job's user as the user, the client as the source address, the system as the target host, Failed for AF.
- IBM's object and attribute keys (objName, fileType, attrName, attrValue, oldAttrValue, fname, filePath, oldObjName, duser, dloName) go to request_parameters and the job, msg, program and sequence to additional_event_data.
- The client is IBM's src (REMOTE_ADDRESS) but Powertech's dst, since Powertech's src is the IBM i itself.
- History log messages (QSYS-QHST) and other Powertech events stay generic.

Time:
- RFC 5424 times carry their offset; RFC 3164 times have no zone and are read as UTC in the current year, so send RFC 5424 or keep the system in UTC.
- In a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 the engine read the time of an RFC 3164 header that follows <PRI> and a space, where the emulator uses the ingest time, so the parser reads RFC 3164 times itself.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow IBM's DISPLAY_JOURNAL examples and key table and Powertech's manual samples.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (98 of 98 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and each also passed as a separate parser under its parent (94 of 94 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 3 Run Tests.
